title: Tropical development odds drop, but coastal flooding is still expected

 The chances of development are decreasing with the system off the east coast but coastal impacts are still expected
 Advertisement Updated: 7:16 PM CST Nov 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jordan West Meteorologist Derek Sibley Meteorologist Tropical development chances drops to low off the southeast coast
 The chances of development are decreasing with the system off the east coast but coastal impacts are still expected
 Updated: 7:16 PM CST Nov 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jordan West Meteorologist Derek Sibley Meteorologist A complex and large low pressure system includes three low pressure centers, one over the Gulf, another over west-central Florida, and a third a few hundred miles east-northeast of the northwestern Bahamas. 
 All of these systems are currently non-tropical. However, the system over the western Atlantic still has some potential to acquire subtropical or tropical characteristics over the next day or two while it moves northward, passing near the North Carolina and mid-Atlantic coasts on Sunday. 
 Advertisement Hearst Owned Tracking The Tropics Although the chances of subtropical or tropical development appear to be decreasing, this large weather system is still expected to produce gusty winds, dangerous surf, rip currents and coastal flooding along portions of the southeast and mid-Atlantic U.S. coasts into early next week. 
 Heavy rain and flash flooding will continue across portions of the northeast Florida tonight, spreading northward over coastal portions of the Carolinas and the mid-Atlantic over the weekend. 
 Interests along the eastern coast of the U.S. should continue to monitor the progress of this system.
 Chance of development over 1-2 days: Low, 30%.
Chance of development over 3-7 days: Low, 30%.
 This system poses no threat to southeast Louisiana or south Mississippi.
